title: Right to erasure - how individuals can actually exercise it
p1:
Think your personal data disappears just because you delete your account? Not necessarily.

Deleting an account and asking an organisation to erase your personal data are two different things.
p2: The right to erasure can allow an individual to ask an organisation to delete personal information in certain circumstances. But it is not an unlimited right. Some data may legally need to be retained, such as records required for compliance or legal claims.
p3:
The practical step is simple: identify the organisation holding your data and make a clear written erasure request. State what information you want deleted and, where possible, the account, service, or records involved. Keep a copy of the request and any response.

One useful detail many people miss: you generally do not have to rely on a website's 'delete account' button. A formal data-erasure request can be a separate exercise of your rights, depending on the law that applies to you.
conclusion: If a company refused to erase your personal data, would you know what to ask for next—or would you simply accept the refusal?
